thesis: The speakers argue that while AI agents have recently evolved to perform long-running tasks autonomously, creating a sensation similar to working with a human team member, the output is often flawed in subtle ways that require human oversight. They suggest that the fundamental economic shift involves moving from automating measurable tasks to focusing on high-leverage decisions that push beyond the boundaries of what is currently known or recorded.
